item: cipher, TYPE:IMAGE, ~92 of 100 sampled hits after excluding known noise regexes
reason: dominant sense across the whole set is heraldic/royal "cipher" = a monogram or royal insignia (Swedish Army Museum "namnchiffer" on uniforms/punches/flags, V&A porcelain/silverware "crowned cipher", funerary "cippe"/"cipe" false match on the French word for a boundary stone); also WWII-era cryptographic hardware already documented as museum objects (Enigma, Siemens Geheimschreiber T52e, Hagelin CD-55) and modern encryption devices (Telekrypt Mini, file-encryption software) -- none is manuscript correspondence

same royal/heraldic-monogram sense dominates in English specifically ("The Royal Cypher", "Coronation Mug with mistake in Cypher", V&A/Royal Museums Greenwich porcelain and jewellery with a monarch's cypher) plus Portable Antiquities Scheme trade-weight/token records (crown+cypher maker's marks) -- no correspondence

item: cifra, cijfer, "en chiffres" -- dominant senses, TYPE:IMAGE
reason: cifra (Spanish/Italian/Romanian) is overwhelmingly the numeral/digit sense (coin legends "monede"/"poltură", scale figures, a "0"-as-letter pun) as already documented for round 1; "cijfer" (Dutch) is Dutch "digit/numeral" on coins, guild tokens, lead seals, Roman-numeral marks; "en chiffres" (French) is the clock-face/route-distance idiom ("cadran... en chiffres arabes/romains", "distances en chiffres") -- confirms and extends the existing noise-pattern list to the image domain in three more languages
